requirements.evidence: All endpoints, the middleware, the command, the models/factories, config, the phpunit pins, CORS and the docs are implemented to the contract: auth 400/401/200 with the entity pair (TotemAuthController.php:109-175), transaction + lockForUpdate (:116-142), throttle 10/30 with a rate_limited renderer (routes/api.php:7,12; bootstrap/app.php:792-798), the JWT ∩ preset scope intersection (TotemAuth.php:403-407), entity 403 / queue 404 / scope 403 (TotemQueueController.php:310-349), 1-based order (:225), IssueTicket with channel Totem (:294). Gaps: the pairing command does not handle a collision with another preset's unique login_code (TotemPairingCode.php:66-72), and if the secret is missing the code is consumed before JWT signing throws.

conventions.evidence: Writes go through IssueTicket (not duplicated). Migrations have generator-style timestamps and a reversible down(). Models declare #[Fillable]. Docs updated (docs/api/totem.md, architecture.md, database-schema.md), plus a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased. Input checks are hand-written rather than $request->validate(), which the custom error codes justify. Authorization is a custom device middleware rather than policies; that is reasonable for device JWT auth.

security.evidence: HS256 verify uses hash_equals and checks alg and exp (TotemJwt.php:631-649). Same 401 for every pairing failure (no oracle). Codes come from random_int. The code is never logged (TotemPairingCode.php:74-77). Entity, preset and totem are cross-checked on every call (TotemAuth.php:392-401). Queues are resolved within the entity only. CORS uses anchored loopback patterns with no credentials (config/cors.php:828-839). Minor: a consumed or expired code keeps occupying the unique column and is only matched by value, which is acceptable.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/TotemApiTest.php covers format/401 variants, single use, both throttles, missing/tampered/expired tokens, inactive totem and preset, entity forgery, heartbeat, scope intersection after detach, 403/404/422 paths, sequential A001/A002 with channel totem, invalid priority creating nothing, and CORS allow/deny. TotemPairingCodeTest covers generate, regenerate and unknown. Missing: assertions on the audit logs, on the printed code, and on a totem/preset entity mismatch with consistent claims. The regenerate test (:1872) is probabilistically flaky (1e-6).

simplicity.evidence: Small dependency-free JWT helper (allowed by the task) and a single priorities source reused by both endpoints. TotemPriorities::values() (:740-743) is unused. resolveEntity/resolveQueue return a union of model|JsonResponse instead of aborting, which adds instanceof checks at each call site.

readability.evidence: Clear names and focused methods; the middleware docblock explains the checks. The model|JsonResponse union return pattern (TotemQueueController.php:202-206, 238-244) is slightly awkward; otherwise consistent with sibling style.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task. The doc mermaid participant rename (docs/api/totem.md:1150-1160) and the 'called_by_user_id' doc fix are tiny doc corrections inside the doc the task required updating.

issues.explanation: The random code is saved into a unique column with no retry, so a collision with another preset's still-stored code (consumed codes are never cleared) throws a QueryException instead of generating a new code.
JWT signing happens after the transaction commits, so a missing secret (LogicException) consumes the code and creates a totem but returns a 500.
No test asserts the audit log entries (pairing success/failure, code generation), that the code is never logged, or that the command prints the code.
Asserting the regenerated code differs from '123456' can fail randomly (1 in 1,000,000).
Returning Model|JsonResponse unions forces instanceof checks at each call site; throwing an HttpResponseException would be more direct.

review.summary: Implements the full totem BFF: migrations/models/factories, the pairing command, transactional pairing login with a hand-rolled but correct HS256 JWT, a validating middleware with live scope intersection, the three endpoints reusing IssueTicket, throttles rendering rate_limited, loopback CORS, and synchronized docs/changelog, all backed by broad feature tests. Only minor issues remain (unhandled pairing-code collisions, the code consumed before signing, no tests for the audit logs), so it would be approved with nits.
